questions.q: According to the summary, what is the ultimate aim behind everything people pursue?
a: The pursuit of happiness
Money and status
Fame and respect
Power and influence
questions.why: Lesson 1 argues that any other reason we give for our actions is merely a step toward happiness.

questions.q: Which outlook on the present and future does the summary call the best one?
a: Enjoying the present while acting for a better future
Seeking maximum pleasure now and ignoring tomorrow
Suffering now in exchange for pleasure later
Showing little interest in either the present or future
questions.why: Lesson 2 contrasts four outlooks and endorses finding joy now while making choices that benefit the future.

questions.q: What did Seligman and Diener find set very happy people apart from less happy ones?
a: Deep bonds with family, friends and partners
Higher incomes and more impressive jobs
More travel and a wider range of experiences
Better physical health and fitness levels
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the main difference was that happier people had strong connections with those around them.

questions.q: Why does the summary criticize the habit of chasing one achievement after another?
a: It keeps postponing happiness to a future milestone
It makes people too content with what they have
It leaves too little time for rest and recovery
It discourages people from setting clear goals
questions.why: Lesson 2 says society teaches us to suffer now for a later reward, which only makes us miserable.

questions.q: Which kind of relationship does David Myers identify as a strong predictor of happiness?
a: A lasting intimate partnership
A large circle of casual friends
A close bond with coworkers
Frequent contact with extended family
questions.why: Lesson 3 cites Myers finding that an intimate lifelong relationship is one of the greatest predictors of happiness.
